clue.text: Where anybody interested can watch the stars come out

definitions.text: Where anybody interested can watch the stars come out

parts.words: Where anybody interested can watch the stars come out
parts.note: reads like astronomy, but the stars are actors and singers leaving a theatre by the performers' exit, where fans wait

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stargazing at night; the stars are celebrities emerging from the backstage entrance of a theatre, where autograph hunters gather.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans wait at a theatre's performers' entrance to see famous actors leave after a show.

clue.text: Dispute the profit, for example

parts.note: profit means gain
say is used to introduce an example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'

explanation.surface: Someone challenges how big the profit really was, giving an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, which is to dispute a claim.

clue.text: They look like sticks, being so badly paid — shame!

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters of the two words beside it are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Workers so poorly paid they look like sticks: a disgrace!
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges PAID and SHAME together; the definition is the family name of stick insects, so 'They' is plural like a family of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the zoological family of stick insects, creatures that mimic twigs for camouflage.

clue.text: Stone, a well-qualified person's to shift around

indicators.note: around tells us the change word goes on the outside, wrapped about the other letters

parts.note: to shift something is to alter it
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate, a qualified person; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A stone that a highly qualified person has to move about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts A, BA (Bachelor of Arts) and S from the 's inside ALTER, giving AL-ABAS-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft white mineral, a kind of stone used for carving.

clue.text: Notorious gunmen turning up, deliver a tirade

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters of gunmen are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British army's gunners
to rant is to deliver a long angry speech

explanation.surface: Notorious gunmen show up and launch into an angry speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery are the British army's gunners, so 'gunmen' are the RA, read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means out-and-out or utter, as in an arrant knave, someone notorious for it.

clue.text: People prepared to deal with one if troublesome — curb one's excitement

definitions.text: People prepared to deal with one if troublesome

indicators.note: the excitement of the words is their being stirred up, so their letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the 's giving an S

explanation.surface: Advice to a rowdy drinker: rein in your excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitement' rearranges CURB and ONES; here 'one' in the definition is any person who causes trouble at a club door.
explanation.definitionFit: Doormen at a club stand ready to throw out any guest who causes trouble.

clue.text: Boards as a member of the family

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or ship is to step on to it
a husband's or wife's son from an earlier marriage is a relative by marriage

explanation.walkthrough: Split one way it is a phrasal verb, 'steps on', meaning gets aboard; read as one word it is a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on a vessel means stepping on it; a spouse's son from a previous marriage is a relative.

clue.text: An individual of some discrimination writing poetry on a river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above, so before, the second

parts.note: an epic is a long piece of narrative poetry
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A discerning person composing verse on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular; 'discrimination' here is discernment of taste, not prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of refined taste in food and drink discriminates carefully between dishes and wines.

clue.text: The trainer will find non-alcoholic drink dear in France

parts.note: tea is a non-alcoholic drink
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: A coach is going to get a cup of tea while in expensive France.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instructs or coaches pupils is a trainer of them.

clue.text: Antipodean seaport and coastal area row

parts.note: a dune is a sand hill by the coast
a row, rhyming with cow, is a din, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A harbour town down under, with its beaches and a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is the noise sense, rhyming with cow, not a line or rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on New Zealand's South Island has a port, and New Zealand is part of the Antipodes.

clue.text: Stage in raising a shrub

indicators.note: raising, building up the words anew, signals that the letters of the two words beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A phase in the cultivation of a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' rearranges STAGE and IN; the surface makes it sound like a step in growing a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the botanical genus of broom, a yellow-flowered bush.

clue.text: He saw himself as most adorable — such a bloomer!

definitions.text: He saw himself as most adorable
definitions.meaning: the youth of Greek myth who fell in love with his own reflection in a pool
a bloomer here is a flowering plant, the daffodil family

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a thing that blooms: the flower named after the vain youth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek youth who loved his reflection gave his name to the daffodil genus of flowers.

clue.text: Rises for a fool occupied by money

indicators.note: occupied by means the first word's letters are filled up from within by another piece

parts.note: an ass is a fool
a cent is a small coin, money

explanation.surface: A fool lands in a cushy job thanks to cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'Rises' looks like a verb but is a plural noun, climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbs or upward movements are rises, as in the ascents of a mountain.

clue.text: Quotidian recorders

parts.note: people who write down events every day, quotidian meaning daily, not musical recorders

explanation.definitionFit: People who keep a journal write in it every day, recording each day's events.

clue.text: It appears right to provoke the park-keeper

parts.note: to anger someone is to provoke them

explanation.surface: It seems right to wind up the park warden.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden who looks after a national park or forest is a ranger.

clue.text: Attending the trial, being a witness

parts.note: at means present at, attending, as in at the trial
a trial is a test, so the trial is the testing

explanation.surface: Someone at court for the hearing, giving evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed answer ends in S, an OCR slip for G: AT plus TESTING makes the real word.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to something, certifying that it is true.

clue.text: Torn about cribbed articles, showing contrition

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go round the outside of the others

parts.note: rent means torn, as in a rent garment
cribbed means confined or pent up
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Ripped up over plagiarised pieces of writing, feeling sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cribbed' suggests copying and 'articles' newspaper pieces, but they mean confined and the single article A.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is sorry for wrongdoing is penitent, showing remorse.

clue.text: Bats are incorrectly placed side by side

indicators.note: incorrectly placed tells us the letters of the two words before it are set in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bats roosting in the wrong place are next to one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly placed' rearranges BATS and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things level with each other, in a line facing forward, are alongside one another.

clue.text: Flourish as a result of high-fibre food

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal, a high-fibre food
a dish is food prepared for a meal

explanation.surface: Thriving as a result of eating a fibre-rich diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' looks like thrive, but it means wave something about with a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a sword is to wave it about, to flourish it.

clue.text: One not to be honoured for presenting the queen with an animal

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
an otter is a river animal

explanation.surface: A man denied an honour for giving the Queen a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: R is Regina, the queen, as in ER. 'honoured' suggests a royal honour, but it is respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is a cad, a person beneath respect.

clue.text: Making a speech on retaining proportion

indicators.note: retaining means the first word keeps another piece held within it

parts.note: a ratio is a proportion

explanation.surface: A speaker carries on while keeping things in proportion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the act of speaking rather than the speech itself, a loose but common equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal address to an audience is the speech someone makes.

clue.text: Gossip later perhaps about a great race

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go round the outside of the race letters
perhaps suggests later is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Gossip about a famous race will come later, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns the letters of later into TALER; the great race is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is someone who chatters about others' affairs, a gossip.

clue.text: Totally grey make-up is required for such sensitivity

parts.note: all means totally, as in all alone

indicators.note: the make-up of grey means its letters are made up again, rearranged

explanation.surface: Wearing cosmetics that are all grey is needed for touchy skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' rearranges GREY into ERGY; it suggests cosmetics, which could cause skin sensitivity.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is a bodily sensitivity to certain substances.

clue.text: This Tory is a real sportsman

parts.note: true means real, genuine
a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: This Conservative is a genuine athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman; blue is also the Conservative party colour, and a staunch Tory is a true blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch, loyal Conservative is called a true blue after the party colour.

clue.text: A crack about fortified wine

parts.note: re means about, concerning
port is a wine fortified with brandy

explanation.surface: A joke about strong wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a joke or a split, but it is a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a sharp loud noise, like the crack of a gun.

clue.text: An Oriental may shade quarters

parts.note: can means may, is allowed to
a tone is a shade of colour
S and E are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An Asian person might paint in hues for living areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' are compass points, here S and E, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Canton, now Guangzhou in southern China, is from the East.

clue.text: Invalid puff about obligation

indicators.note: about means the breathing word's letters go round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: to pant is to puff, breathe hard
a tie is a bond or obligation

explanation.surface: An ailing person gasping over a duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as not valid, but it is a sick person, stressed on the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill and receiving medical care is an invalid, stressed on the first syllable.

clue.text: An entitlement to beef?

parts.note: reads like a right to complain, but a title, a knighthood, is given to a cut of beef, from the tale of a king knighting a joint of meat

explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like a grumble; the legend says a king was so pleased with a loin of beef he knighted it, giving a title.
explanation.definitionFit: This cut of beef from the upper loin is said to have been knighted by a king.

clue.text: Sailors holding on maybe get to see Nobel prize winner

indicators.note: holding means the sailors' letters go round the outside, gripping the rest

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is sailors

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of get could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Sailors clinging on might get to see a laureate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges get into TGE. Wilhelm Röntgen, discoverer of X-rays, won the first physics Nobel; the umlaut is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Röntgen won the first Nobel Prize in physics, in 1901, for discovering X-rays.

clue.text: No government supporter!

parts.note: reads like an opponent of the ruling party, but it is someone who supports having no government at all

explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism advocates abolishing the state, so its followers back a world without rulers.
